initialize.t: We start from a blank guess: **w = 0, b = 0** (a flat line along the bottom) with **learning rate η = 0.1**. Training will improve it step by step.

predict.t: Predict every house with the current line **ŷ = w·x + b**. With w = 0 and b = 0, every prediction is **0**.

measure-error.t: The residuals **ŷ − y** are −2.0, −2.8, −3.7, −4.1 and −5.2, so the **MSE is huge: 13.876**. The line is far below every house.

compute-gradients.t: The slopes of the MSE are **∂MSE/∂w = −15.78** and **∂MSE/∂b = −7.12**. Both are negative, so **raising w and b lowers the MSE**.

update-w.t: **w ← w − η·∂MSE/∂w = 0 − 0.1 × (−15.78) = 1.578.** Stepping against the gradient tilts the line upward.

update-b.t: **b ← b − η·∂MSE/∂b = 0 − 0.1 × (−7.12) = 0.712.** Both parameters are updated together, from the same residuals.

new-line.t: After one round the line passes through the houses, and the **MSE has dropped from 13.876 to 0.1122**.

repeat.t: **Predict, measure, compute gradients, update**, again and again. The line settles quickly and the MSE falls by orders of magnitude.

trained-line.t: After 500 rounds: **w = 1.54, b = 0.48, MSE 0.0166**. This is the least-squares line. **Training is just this loop, run many times.**
